chapters.title: Do Not Uncover
chapters.html:
Leviticus 18

Not Like Egypt, Not Like Canaan

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: I am the LORD your God.

3You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived; and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; and you shall not walk in their statutes.

4You shall carry out My rulings and keep My statutes, and walk in them. I am the LORD your God.

5You shall keep My statutes and My rulings; the person who does them shall live by them. I am the LORD.

Whose Nakedness Is Not to Be Uncovered

6No man shall come near to anyone of his own flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.

7You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

8You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It is your father's nakedness.

9You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born outside.

10You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because their nakedness is your own.

11You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.

12You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She is your father's flesh.

13You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's flesh.

14You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother — you shall not come near his wife. She is your aunt.

15You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

16You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It is your brother's nakedness.

17You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are her own flesh. It is depravity.

18You shall not take a woman together with her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness while she is alive.

And These

19You shall not come near a woman in the uncleanness of her monthly separation, to uncover her nakedness.

20You shall not lie with your neighbor's wife and so become unclean by her.

21You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech; and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

22You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is detestable.

23You shall not lie with any animal and so become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal to mate with it. It is a mixing.

What the Land Does

24Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these, because by all of these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.

25The land became unclean, and I punished it for its guilt, and the land vomited out those living in it.

26But you shall keep My statutes and My rulings, and shall not do any of these detestable things — neither the native nor the guest living among you —

27because the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.

28Otherwise, when you make the land unclean, it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

29For whoever does any of these detestable things — those who do them shall be cut off from among their people.

30You shall keep My charge, not to do any of the detestable statutes that were done before you, and not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."

Notes

  • v6 "uncover nakedness" — gallot ervah, and the phrase runs through the chapter twenty-four times, so this rendering keeps it identical every time the Hebrew repeats it. Ervah is exposure, the state of being uncovered, and the idiom is a euphemism for sexual relations — Hebrew names the act by naming the shame of being seen. The chapter is built out of one sentence said over and over with the relative changed, which is why it reads like a list rather than an argument.

  • v6 "his own flesh" — she'er besaro, and she'er means both flesh and a blood relative, with no line drawn between the senses. The chapter uses it as its whole principle: these people are not other people, they are you. Verse 10 makes it explicit about a granddaughter — their nakedness is your own.

  • vv7–8 the father's nakedness — twice the text describes an offense against a woman as an offense against a man: the father's wife is your father's nakedness (v8), the brother's wife is your brother's nakedness (v16). The women in those two verses are not blood relatives at all. What the formula tracks in these cases is the marriage, not the bloodline, and it says so by naming the husband.

  • v18 "a woman together with her sister" — ishah el achotah, and this is the hardest verse in the chapter to be sure of. The phrase occurs in seven other places in the Hebrew Bible and in every one of them it is a fixed idiom meaning one to another, used of things: the curtains of the tabernacle coupled one to another (Exodus 26:3, 5, 6), the frames (26:17), the wings of the living creatures touching one another (Ezekiel 1:9, 23; 3:13). Not one of them is about a woman. So this verse can be read as forbidding marriage to a wife's sister — which is what Jacob did, and the word litsror, as a rival, points that way — or as forbidding taking one woman in addition to another at all. The two readings produce two different laws, and the Hebrew supports both.

  • v21 the one prohibition that is not sexual — le-ha'avir la-Molekh, to make pass over to Molech, dropped without transition into the middle of a list about relatives. The verb is avar, to cross over; what the passing consists of is not stated here, though 20:14 and later books use fire. And the sentence that follows it is about speech: you shall not profane the name of your God. Nothing in the chapter explains why this belongs here.

  • v22 "as one lies with a woman" — mishkevei ishah, and the noun is plural: the lyings of a woman. The same plural appears in the parallel at 20:13 and nowhere else in the Bible, and what the plural is doing has never been settled. The verse ends with to'evah, the word Genesis uses for Egyptians eating with Hebrews (43:32) and for shepherds (46:34) — a term for what a given community will not have among it, which is a different kind of word from tamei, unclean, and from sheqets, loathsome, which chapter 11 used of animals.

  • v23 "It is a mixing" — tevel, built on a root for mixing or confounding, and the sense is the running together of things that belong to separate categories. That is the same logic as chapter 11's clean and unclean animals and 19:19's ban on sowing a field with two kinds of seed: the offense named is not cruelty or harm but confusion of kinds. The word occurs in this sense twice in the Bible, here and at 20:12.

  • v23 the woman's clause — the verse addresses a man and then turns and addresses a woman in the same breath, and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal. It is the only sentence in the chapter with a woman as the subject of the prohibition rather than its object. Everything else here is said to men about women.

  • vv25, 28 "the land vomited out" — va-taqi ha-arets, from qi, to vomit, and it is a physical verb used of a sick body. This is the only place in the Torah where the land is the one who acts. Not God expelling the Canaanites, not Israel conquering them: the ground itself is made nauseous and throws off what is on it. And v28 turns it on the audience — the land will not vomit you out — which means the new occupants are being told they are on probation with the same soil.

  • v3 Egypt and Canaan, named together — the chapter opens by naming both the country they came out of and the country they are going into, and forbids the practices of each. It does not say what those practices were. Every account of what Egypt or Canaan actually did comes from somewhere other than this text, and the chapter itself simply says: not like the place behind you, not like the place ahead.

  • v5 "and live by them" — va-chai bahem, four words that became one of the most argued sentences in the Bible: the statutes are given so that a person may live by them. Ezekiel 20 quotes the exact phrase three times in one chapter (vv11, 13, 21) and then, at v25, says God gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not live. The Hebrew here says only what it says, and does not define the living.

speech.text: Leviticus 18
Not Like Egypt, Not Like Canaan
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: I am the LORD your God.
You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived; and you shall not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; and you shall not walk in their statutes.
You shall carry out My rulings and keep My statutes, and walk in them. I am the LORD your God.
You shall keep My statutes and My rulings; the person who does them shall live by them. I am the LORD.
Whose Nakedness Is Not to Be Uncovered
No man shall come near to anyone of his own flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the LORD.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It is your father's nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born outside.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because their nakedness is your own.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She is your father's flesh.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's flesh.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother — you shall not come near his wife. She is your aunt.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It is your brother's nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They are her own flesh. It is depravity.
You shall not take a woman together with her sister, as a rival, to uncover her nakedness while she is alive.
And These
You shall not come near a woman in the uncleanness of her monthly separation, to uncover her nakedness.
You shall not lie with your neighbor's wife and so become unclean by her.
You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech; and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is detestable.
You shall not lie with any animal and so become unclean by it; and a woman shall not stand in front of an animal to mate with it. It is a mixing.
What the Land Does
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these, because by all of these the nations I am driving out before you have made themselves unclean.
The land became unclean, and I punished it for its guilt, and the land vomited out those living in it.
But you shall keep My statutes and My rulings, and shall not do any of these detestable things — neither the native nor the guest living among you —
because the people of the land who were before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.
Otherwise, when you make the land unclean, it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
For whoever does any of these detestable things — those who do them shall be cut off from among their people.
You shall keep My charge, not to do any of the detestable statutes that were done before you, and not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."

chapters.title: Love Your Neighbor as Yourself
chapters.html:
Leviticus 19

You Shall Be Holy

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

3Each of you shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.

4Do not turn to worthless gods, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.

5When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.

6It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day, and what is left until the third day shall be burned in the fire.

7If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is foul. It will not be accepted.

8Whoever eats it carries his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from his people.

What You Leave in the Field

9When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping to the edge of your field, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest.

10You shall not strip your vineyard bare, and you shall not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the guest. I am the LORD your God.

How to Treat Each Other

11You shall not steal, and you shall not deal falsely, and you shall not lie to one another.

12You shall not swear falsely by My name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.

13You shall not exploit your neighbor and you shall not rob him. The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning.

14You shall not curse a deaf man, and you shall not put a stumbling block in front of a blind man; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

15You shall not do injustice in judgment. You shall not show favor to the poor or defer to the great. In righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.

16You shall not go around spreading slander among your people. You shall not stand on the blood of your neighbor. I am the LORD.

17You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall be sure to correct your neighbor, and not carry guilt because of him.

18You shall not take revenge and you shall not hold a grudge against the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

Mixtures

19You shall keep My statutes. You shall not mate your livestock with a different kind. You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed. You shall not put on a garment woven of two kinds of material.

20When a man lies with a woman who is a slave promised to another man, and she has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.

21He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting — a ram for a guilt offering.

22The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD, for the sin he has committed; and he shall be forgiven for it.

23When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you shall treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it shall be forbidden to you. It shall not be eaten.

24In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise offering to the LORD.

25In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that it will yield more for you. I am the LORD your God.

Marks on the Body

26You shall not eat anything with the blood in it. You shall not practice divination and you shall not read omens.

27You shall not round off the hair at the sides of your head, and you shall not ruin the edge of your beard.

28You shall not make a gash in your flesh for the dead, and you shall not put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.

29Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with depravity.

30You shall keep My sabbaths and fear My sanctuary. I am the LORD.

31Do not turn to ghosts, and do not seek out spirits, and so become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

The Old, the Foreigner, the Scales

32You shall rise in the presence of the gray-haired and honor the old; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.

33When a guest lives with you in your land, you shall not wrong him.

34The guest living with you shall be to you as a native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, because you were guests in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

35You shall not do injustice in judgment — in measuring length, in weight, or in quantity.

36You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

37You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them. I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv18 and 34 the sentence and its twin — ve-ahavta le-re'akha kamokha, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself, is the most quoted line in Leviticus. Sixteen verses later the identical construction is used again, of somebody else: ve-ahavta lo kamokha, and you shall love him as yourself, said of the ger, the guest living in your land. Those two verses are the only places in the entire Hebrew Bible where this phrase occurs. The famous one has a twin, and the twin is almost never quoted.

  • v18 "love your neighbor" — the Hebrew does not say love your neighbor the way English does. It is ve-ahavta le-re'akha — love to your neighbor, with a preposition where a direct object would be expected. The construction pushes the sense toward acting lovingly toward someone rather than feeling something about them, and it sits at the end of a paragraph made entirely of actions: do not steal, do not withhold wages overnight, do not curse the deaf, do not take revenge. The command arrives as the summary of a list of things to do and not do.

  • v2 who is being addressed — kol adat benei Yisrael, the whole congregation. Everything up to chapter 16 was spoken to Aaron and his sons; the demand to be holy was a priest's job description. Here the same word is handed to everyone, and the chapter that follows is about wages, scales, gleaning, gossip, and the old man you stand up for.

  • vv9–10 what is left in the field — four things: the edge of the field is not reaped, the dropped stalks are not picked up, the vineyard is not stripped, the fallen grapes are not gathered. The poor and the guest are not given anything — they are left something, and they come and take it themselves. This is the law Ruth is working under in Boaz's field, and it is written as a restriction on the owner rather than as a charity.

  • v11 "you shall not lie to one another" — ish ba-amito, the rare word from 6:2, where a man who lies to his amit about a deposit is said to break faith with the LORD. Both verses use the same verb, kachash. Nine of the ten occurrences of amit in the Bible are in Leviticus.

  • v14 the deaf man and the blind man — a curse the deaf man cannot hear, and a stone the blind man cannot see. Both are offenses with no witness and no possibility of retaliation, and the verse ends and you shall fear your God. That formula occurs five times in the Bible, all of them in Leviticus, and every one of the five is attached to a command about someone who cannot fight back: the deaf and blind here, the old man at v32, and at 25:17, 36 and 43 a fellow Israelite in debt or in service.

  • v16 "stand on the blood of your neighbor" — lo ta'amod al dam re'ekha, and what it means is not clear. The preposition can be on, against, beside or over; the phrase might forbid profiting from a neighbor's death, standing by while his life is at risk, or testifying in a capital case. The first half of the verse is about carrying tales, which suggests speech. The Hebrew supports more than one reading and nothing in the verse settles it.

  • v17 "you shall be sure to correct" — hokheach tokhiach, the verb doubled with itself. Yakhach is to argue a case, set someone right, have it out. The verse pairs it with do not hate your brother in your heart: the alternative to silent hatred is saying something. And the clause that follows, and not carry guilt because of him, makes the silence itself the offense — the one who says nothing ends up holding the guilt.

  • v19 "two kinds" — kil'ayim, and the word for the forbidden cloth is sha'atnez, which occurs twice in the Bible, here and at Deuteronomy 22:11 — where it is defined as wool and linen together. The three bans are one idea: no crossbred animals, no mixed seed, no mixed cloth. It is the logic of chapter 11 applied to farming and weaving, and no reason is given here either.

  • v20 the hardest verse in the chapter — two of its words are effectively unrecoverable. Necherefet, describing the woman's status, occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse; it is usually taken as designated or promised to a man. Biqqoret, the consequence, also occurs once in this form, and has been read as an inquiry, a distinction in punishment, and compensation. What the verse plainly says is that the two are not put to death, and that the reason is her legal condition: because she was not free.

  • v23 "you shall treat its fruit as forbidden" — the Hebrew is va-araltem orlato, you shall foreskin its foreskin, the verb taking its own noun, and the noun is the word for the foreskin removed at circumcision. Young fruit is spoken of as uncircumcised, so the tree is under the same language as a child in its first days. English cannot do the doubling and has nothing to do with the image, so the word here is forbidden and the picture is in this note.

  • v28 "tattoo marks" — ketovet qa'aqa, and qa'aqa occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in this verse. It sits beside a ban on gashing the flesh la-nefesh, for the dead — both are mourning practices, cut into the body. The two halves of the verse belong together, and the ban is not on marking as such but on marking oneself over a death.

  • v36 "an honest ephah and an honest hin" — tsedeq four times in one verse, the noun usually rendered righteousness. Applied to scales it means accurate, and the chapter uses one word for both, so that a correct weight and a right action are the same thing. The verse then attaches the exodus to it: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt — the credential offered for a rule about shopkeeping.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.html:
Leviticus 20

Molech, and the Ones Who Look Away

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Say to the sons of Israel: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the guests living in Israel, who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him.

3I Myself will set My face against that man, and cut him off from among his people, because he gave of his children to Molech, and so made My sanctuary unclean and profaned My holy name.

4If the people of the land deliberately shut their eyes to that man when he gives his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,

5then I Myself will set My face against that man and against his family, and cut him off from among their people — him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molech.

6The person who turns to ghosts and to spirits, prostituting himself by following them — I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.

7You shall set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.

8You shall keep My statutes and do them. I am the LORD who makes you holy.

The Penalties

9Any man who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on his own head.

10A man who commits adultery with another man's wife — who commits adultery with his neighbor's wife — the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

11A man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

12A man who lies with his daughter-in-law — both of them shall surely be put to death. They have done a mixing; their blood is on their own heads.

13A man who lies with a male as one lies with a woman — both of them have done a detestable thing. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

14A man who takes a woman and her mother — it is depravity. They shall burn him and them in the fire, so that there shall be no depravity among you.

15A man who lies with an animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.

16A woman who comes near any animal to mate with it — you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

17A man who takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness — it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he carries his guilt.

18A man who lies with a woman in her sickness and uncovers her nakedness — he has laid bare her source, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from among their people.

19You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, because that lays bare his own flesh. They shall carry their guilt.

20A man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They shall carry their sin; they shall die childless.

21A man who takes his brother's wife — it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.

Why You Are Not Like Them

22You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into to live in does not vomit you out.

23You shall not walk in the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was sick of them.

24I said to you: You shall take possession of their ground, and I will give it to you as your own — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

25You shall separate the clean animal from the unclean, and the unclean bird from the clean, and you shall not make yourselves loathsome with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have separated out for you as unclean.

26You shall be holy to Me, because I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.

27A man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them; their blood is on their own heads."

Notes

  • v17 "it is a disgrace" — the Hebrew word is chesed, and this is one of the strangest sentences in the Bible. Chesed is the great covenant word: loyal love, steadfast kindness, the thing God is said to keep for a thousand generations, the word in I desire mercy and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6) and all through the Psalms. Here it names an act punished by being cut off. The spelling is identical and so is the vowel pointing, checked against Hosea 6:6 and Psalm 25:10 — this is not a look-alike. Either one root carried two opposite senses, shame and devotion, or a second root has been swallowed by the first. Nothing in the verse decides it, and the English cannot show the collision, so it is recorded here.

  • v9 "his blood is on his own head" — damav bo, literally his blood is on him, said six times in this chapter. It is not a statement that the man deserves it. It is a liability formula: the blood is accounted to him and not to the people carrying out the sentence. Israelite law returns to this repeatedly — who is answerable for a death — and the phrase settles the question in three words each time.

  • v4 "deliberately shut their eyes" — ha'alem ya'limu, the verb doubled with itself, which is how Hebrew leans on a word: not a failure to notice but a decision not to see. And v5 makes the consequence fall on the man and his family, and on everyone who followed him. The community that looks away is legislated for in the same breath as the offender.

  • v2 "the people of the land shall stone him" — am ha-arets, and there is no court, no priest and no king in this sentence. Execution here is the work of the general population, and the chapter assigns it to them twice (vv2, 27). What the previous chapter asked of them was leaving grain in a field; this one asks this.

  • chapter 18 and chapter 20 are the same list twice — the first time as prohibitions, the second time with what it costs. Almost every offense in 18 reappears here in the same order, now attached to a penalty, and a few drop out. A reader who wants to know what the Torah thought was worst does not get it from the prohibitions; the weighting is only visible here, where death, being cut off, bearing guilt and dying childless are handed out at different levels.

  • vv20–21 "they shall die childless" — aririm, stripped or bare, used of a person with no descendants. It is a different kind of sentence from the ones around it: nobody executes it and no court is involved. For two of the offenses on this list the punishment is simply that the line ends.

  • v21 "it is an impurity" — niddah, the same word used in chapter 15 for a woman's monthly separation, which is a status and involves no wrongdoing at all. Here it is used of an act. The word does not mean uncleanness of a moral kind in chapter 15 and does seem to in this verse, and the Hebrew uses one noun for both.

  • v23 "I was sick of them" — va-aquts bam, from quts, a verb for loathing, the feeling of being unable to stand something any longer. It is the word used of the Egyptians when the Israelites multiplied (Exodus 1:12). This is God saying it about the previous occupants of Canaan, in the first person, with no legal vocabulary attached.

  • vv24–26 "separated" — badal four times in three verses, and it is the verb of Genesis 1, where God separates light from darkness and waters from waters. The chapter's closing argument is built out of it: I separated you from the peoples (v24), so you separate clean animals from unclean (v25), from things I separated out for you (v25), because I separated you to be Mine (v26). The dietary law and the election of Israel are stated as one act, in one word, four times over. It is the same verb handed to the priesthood at 10:10 and used to close chapter 11.

  • v27 "who has a ghost or a spirit in them" — the Hebrew says ki yihyeh vahem, if there is in them, which describes the medium as containing the thing rather than consulting it. The same two words, ov and yidde'oni, appeared at 19:31 as things not to turn to; here they are inside a person. The text never explains what either is.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, because that lays bare his own flesh. They shall carry their guilt.
A man who lies with his uncle's wife has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They shall carry their sin; they shall die childless.
A man who takes his brother's wife — it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness. They shall be childless.
Why You Are Not Like Them
You shall keep all My statutes and all My rulings and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into to live in does not vomit you out.
You shall not walk in the statutes of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I was sick of them.
I said to you: You shall take possession of their ground, and I will give it to you as your own — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

You shall separate the clean animal from the unclean, and the unclean bird from the clean, and you shall not make yourselves loathsome with any animal or bird or anything that creeps on the ground, which I have separated out for you as unclean.
You shall be holy to Me, because I the LORD am holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.
A man or a woman who has a ghost or a spirit in them shall surely be put to death. They shall stone them; their blood is on their own heads."

chapters.title: Rules for the Priests
chapters.html:
Leviticus 21

A Priest and the Dead

1The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: None of them shall make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,

2except for his own flesh closest to him — for his mother and for his father, and for his son and for his daughter and for his brother,

3and for his unmarried sister, who is close to him because she has had no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.

4He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, profaning himself.

5They shall not make a bald patch on their heads, and they shall not shave off the edge of their beards, and they shall not cut a gash in their flesh.

6They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God, because they present the LORD's offerings by fire, the bread of their God. They shall be holy.

7They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or who has been disgraced, and they shall not take a woman divorced from her husband, because he is holy to his God.

8You shall treat him as holy, because he presents the bread of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD, who makes you holy, am holy.

9A priest's daughter, if she profanes herself by prostituting herself, profanes her father. She shall be burned in the fire.

The High Priest

10The priest who is greatest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and whose hand was filled to wear the garments, shall not let his hair hang loose and shall not tear his clothes.

11He shall not go near any dead body. He shall not make himself unclean even for his father or for his mother.

12He shall not go out of the sanctuary and profane the sanctuary of his God, because the crown of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.

13He shall take as his wife a woman who is a virgin.

14A widow, or a divorced woman, or a woman disgraced by prostitution — these he shall not take. He shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife,

15and he shall not profane his offspring among his people, because I am the LORD who makes him holy."

A Blemish

16The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

17"Speak to Aaron, saying: None of your offspring through their generations who has a blemish shall come near to present the bread of his God.

18No man at all who has a blemish shall come near: a man who is blind or lame, or disfigured in the face, or with a limb too long,

19or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,

20or a hunchback, or a withered man, or one with a spot in his eye, or a scab, or a skin eruption, or crushed testicles.

21No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall come forward to present the LORD's offerings by fire. He has a blemish; he shall not come forward to present the bread of his God.

22He may eat the bread of his God, both the most holy and the holy.

23But he shall not come to the veil and shall not come near the altar, because he has a blemish, and he shall not profane My holy places, because I am the LORD who makes them holy."

24Moses spoke this to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the list of who a priest may bury — mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and an unmarried sister. A wife is not on the list. Whether she is covered by the obscure v4, or assumed under his close flesh in v2, or genuinely left out, has been argued for as long as the verse has existed, and the text does not resolve it.

  • v4 the broken verse — lo yittamma ba'al be-ammav le-hechallo, and it is one of the least recoverable sentences in Leviticus. Ba'al means a husband, an owner, a master; be-ammav is among his people; le-hechallo is to profane himself. The words are all ordinary and the sentence they make is not. It has been read as a rule about a priest's wife, about a chief among his kin, and as the conclusion of vv1–3. This rendering follows the words and leaves the difficulty where the Hebrew leaves it.

  • v5 the written and the spoken text — the consonants say yiqrechah, singular, and the reading tradition says yiqrechu, plural. It is one of only five places in Leviticus where the two part company; two of the others are Aaron's hand at 9:22 and at 16:21. Nothing turns on it here, which is itself worth seeing: these variants are usually this small.

  • v5 the same three mourning customs, again — a bald patch, a shaved beard-edge, a gash in the flesh. Two chapters ago the identical practices were forbidden to everyone (19:27–28). Here they are forbidden to priests specifically, in almost the same words. The Torah often legislates twice at two levels, and comparing the two tells you which audience each law was aimed at.

  • vv6, 8, 17, 21, 22 "the bread of their God" — lechem eloheihem, the same startling phrase as 3:11, where what goes up from the altar is called God's food. It is used five times in this chapter, always at the moment of saying what a priest is for: he is the one who brings God his bread. Nothing in these verses softens it.

  • v9 the priest's daughter — the harshest sentence in the chapter, and it falls on someone who is not a priest and cannot become one. The stated reason is entirely about her father: she profanes her father. Whatever holiness he carries is treated here as something her conduct can damage, and the penalty is the one given at 20:14 for depravity.

  • v10 "the priest who is greatest among his brothers" — ha-kohen ha-gadol, the great priest, which is where English gets high priest. Chapter 4 called the same office ha-kohen ha-mashiach, the anointed priest. Two titles for one man, and this one is about rank among his brothers rather than about oil.

  • vv10–11 forbidden to mourn at all — an ordinary priest may bury his own mother and father (v2). The high priest may not, and may not let his hair down or tear his clothes. That is exactly what Aaron and his surviving sons were forbidden at 10:6 on the day Nadab and Abihu died — the same two verbs. What was an emergency order in chapter 10 is written here as the permanent condition of the office.

  • vv18–20 the list nobody can fully translate — twelve conditions, and several of the words are effectively unknown. Tevallul occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, in v20. Sarua occurs twice, both in Leviticus, and is usually taken as a limb of the wrong length. Charum is guessed from a root for cutting, so a damaged face. The English in every Bible is a reconstruction from roots and from the company the words keep, and the confident-sounding lists in modern translations are covering a good deal of uncertainty.

  • vv22–23 what he keeps — a priest with a blemish is not put out of the priesthood and not cut off from his family's living. He eats the holy food, including the most holy portions, which is the priests' sustenance and their inheritance in place of land. What he cannot do is approach the altar or the veil. The distinction the chapter draws is between being a priest and performing at the altar, and it draws it in two verses without explanation.

chapters.title: Who May Eat the Holy Things
chapters.html:
Leviticus 22

The Priests and the Holy Things

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they keep themselves apart from the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they set apart for Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.

3Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your offspring who comes near to the holy things that the sons of Israel set apart for the LORD while he is unclean — that person shall be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.

4No man at all of the offspring of Aaron who has blight or a discharge shall eat of the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by a dead person, or a man who has an emission of semen,

5or a man who touches any swarming thing that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean, whatever his uncleanness —

6the person who touches any of these shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat of the holy things unless he has washed his body in water.

7When the sun goes down he will be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.

8He shall not eat an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and so make himself unclean by it. I am the LORD.

9They shall keep My charge, so that they do not carry sin because of it and die for profaning it. I am the LORD who makes them holy.

10No outsider shall eat a holy thing. A priest's resident or a hired man shall not eat a holy thing.

11But if a priest buys a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and so may those born in his house; they may eat of his bread.

12A priest's daughter who is married to an outsider shall not eat of the holy contributions.

13But a priest's daughter who is widowed or divorced, and has no child, and has come back to her father's house as in her youth, may eat of her father's bread. But no outsider shall eat of it.

14If a man eats a holy thing by mistake, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing back to the priest.

15They shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they raise up to the LORD,

16and so make them carry guilt that must be paid for, by eating their holy things. For I am the LORD who makes them holy."

An Offering Must Be Whole

17The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

18"Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them: Any man at all of the house of Israel, or of the guests living in Israel, who brings his offering for any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings, which they bring to the LORD as a burnt offering —

19to be accepted for you, it must be an unblemished male, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.

20Anything that has a blemish you shall not bring, because it will not be accepted for you.

21If a man brings a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD to fulfill a special vow, or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be unblemished to be accepted. There shall be no blemish in it.

22Blind, or broken, or maimed, or with a wart, or a scab, or a skin eruption — you shall not bring these to the LORD, and you shall not put an offering by fire from them on the altar to the LORD.

23You may offer as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short, but it will not be accepted for a vow.

24You shall not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, or crushed, or torn, or cut, and in your land you shall not do this.

25You shall not take any of these from a foreigner and offer them as the bread of your God, because their ruin is in them; there is a blemish in them. They will not be accepted for you."

The Eighth Day

26The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

27"When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it will be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.

28Whether ox or sheep, you shall not slaughter it and its young on the same day.

29When you offer a thanksgiving sacrifice to the LORD, offer it so that it is accepted for you.

30It shall be eaten on that same day; you shall leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.

31You shall keep My commandments and do them. I am the LORD.

32You shall not profane My holy name, and I will be shown holy among the sons of Israel. I am the LORD who makes you holy,

33who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."

Notes

  • v2 "keep themselves apart" — ve-yinnazru, from nazar, the root of nazir, the Nazirite who separates himself to the LORD (Numbers 6:2). The men who handle the holy things every day are told to hold back from them whenever they are unclean. Closeness is not a standing right; it is renewed each time they are clean.

  • v3 "cut off from My presence" — mi-lefanai, from before My face. Every other time Leviticus says what a person is cut off from, it is his people (7:20, 17:4, 20:17, and eleven more). Here, for a priest, the loss is named differently: not his people, but the face of God.

  • vv10–11 the slave eats; the hired man does not — the line is drawn around the household, not around freedom. A man the priest bought with his money belongs to the priest's house and eats its bread; a hired man, free and paid, only works for it and does not. The Passover draws the same line in the same words: the bought slave may eat, a resident and a hired man shall not (Exodus 12:44–45).

  • vv12–13 the priest's daughter — marriage to a man outside the priesthood takes her out of the house that eats the holy portion. If she is widowed or divorced with no child and comes back as in her youth, ki-ne'ureha, she is at her father's table again and the right comes back with her. Belonging here is not blood alone; it is whose bread you eat.

  • v14 "add a fifth" — the same repayment as 5:16 for sinning against the holy thing: the value in full, one fifth more, given to the priest.

  • v21 "to fulfill a special vow" — le-falle neder, and the verb is from pala, the root of pele, wonder: the word of 15:11 in Exodus, doing wonders. The same verb opens the law of vows in 27:2. The sense is a vow set apart as extraordinary, beyond the ordinary gift.

  • v22 "with a wart" — yabbelet occurs here and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. The Greek has myrmēkiōnta, warted; the other old reading is a running sore, and with one occurrence in a list, nothing in the Hebrew settles it. Scab and skin eruption are the two words of 21:20: the same faults that keep a priest from the altar keep an animal off it.

  • v24 "in your land you shall not do this" — the Hebrew does not say what this is. It can mean do not offer such animals, which repeats the first half of the verse, or do not do this to animals at all, which would forbid gelding. Both readings are old, and the words allow either.

  • v25 "a foreigner" — ben nekhar, a son of a foreign land, and not the same person as the ger of v18, the guest living in Israel, who may bring his own offerings. The man from outside may not supply the animal. Their ruin is in them is mashchatam, from shachat, the verb used of all flesh that had ruined its way before the flood (Genesis 6:12).

  • v27 "from the eighth day on" — seven days with its mother, and on the eighth day it may be offered: the rule for a firstling in Exodus 22:30, now for every animal. The eighth day is the day of a boy's circumcision (12:3) and the day the priests' ordination was complete and their service began (9:1). In this book the eighth day is the day something is first given over to God.

  • v28 "it and its young" — oto ve-et beno, it and its son. The law does not say mother or father; it forbids killing a parent and its offspring on the same day.

  • v32 "I will be shown holy" — ve-niqdashti, the form Moses used at the death of Nadab and Abihu: through those near Me I will be shown holy (10:3). The chapter turns on one pair of words: profane, chillel, four times (vv2, 9, 15, 32), against holy. God's name is either profaned or shown holy by how Israel handles what belongs to Him.

chapters.title: The Appointed Times
chapters.html:
Leviticus 23

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: The appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies — these are My appointed times.

The Sabbath

3Work may be done for six days, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You shall do no work at all. It is a sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.

Passover and Unleavened Bread

4These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies, which you shall proclaim at their appointed time.

5In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, between the evenings, is the LORD's Passover.

6On the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.

7On the first day you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

8You shall present an offering by fire to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work."

The First Sheaf

9The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

10"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest.

11He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, so that it is accepted for you. On the day after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.

12On the day you wave the sheaf you shall offer an unblemished lamb a year old as a burnt offering to the LORD,

13and its grain offering, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a soothing aroma; and its drink offering, wine, a fourth of a hin.

14You shall eat no bread, roasted grain or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

Fifty Days

15You shall count for yourselves from the day after the sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the wave offering: there shall be seven full sabbaths.

16Until the day after the seventh sabbath you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.

17From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of bread for waving, made of two tenths of fine flour. They shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

18With the bread you shall present seven unblemished lambs a year old, and one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire, a soothing aroma to the LORD.

19You shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two lambs a year old as a sacrifice of peace offerings.

20The priest shall wave them before the LORD with the bread of the firstfruits, together with the two lambs. They shall be holy to the LORD, for the priest.

21On that very day you shall proclaim a holy assembly for yourselves. You shall do no ordinary work. It is a lasting statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

22When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap all the way to the edge of your field, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and for the guest. I am the LORD your God."

The First of the Seventh Month

23The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

24"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a rest, a remembrance with horn blasts, a holy assembly.

25You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD."

The Day of Atonement

26The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

27"But on the tenth of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy assembly for you, and you shall afflict yourselves, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD.

28You shall do no work at all on that very day, because it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.

29For any person who does not afflict himself on that very day shall be cut off from his people.

30Any person who does any work at all on that very day — I will destroy that person from among his people.

31You shall do no work at all. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

32It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. On the ninth of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your sabbath."

Booths

33The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

34"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths, seven days to the LORD.

35On the first day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

36For seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a closing assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

37These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, for presenting offerings by fire to the LORD — burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day —

38besides the LORD's sabbaths, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings, which you give to the LORD.

39But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall keep the festival of the LORD seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day is a rest.

40On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.

41You shall keep it as a festival to the LORD seven days in the year. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall keep it.

42You shall live in booths for seven days. Every native Israelite shall live in booths,

43so that your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

44Moses told the sons of Israel the appointed times of the LORD.

Notes

  • v2 "appointed times… holy assemblies" — mo'adim, from ya'ad, to fix a meeting: the word of the tent of meeting, ohel mo'ed, and of the lights in Genesis 1:14, set in the sky for appointed times. The calendar is a set of meetings with God, and the sun and moon were made to keep them. Holy assembly is miqra qodesh, from qara, to call: a holy calling. The verb in the same verse is which you shall call them, so the day is named for the summons that gathers the people.

  • v3 "You shall do no work at all" — the chapter uses two different rules and keeps them apart every time. On the sabbath and the Day of Atonement it is kol melakhah, any work at all (vv3, 28, 30, 31). On every festival day it is melekhet avodah, ordinary work, the work of a trade (vv7, 8, 21, 25, 35, 36), which is why Exodus 12:16 could let food be made on the first day of Unleavened Bread. Only the two days of total rest are called sabbath of complete rest.

  • v10 "the sheaf" — omer, which in Exodus 16 was a measure of manna, one per person each day. Here it is a sheaf of standing grain, and the first one belongs to God before anyone eats bread from the new harvest (v14).

  • v11 "on the day after the sabbath" — the text does not say which sabbath: the weekly Sabbath, or the first day of Unleavened Bread (v7), which is kept like one. The two readings put the sheaf, and the fifty days that are counted from it, on different dates, and later Jewish communities divided over exactly this line.

  • vv15–16 "seven full sabbaths… fifty days" — sabbath here also means the week it closes. Seven weeks are counted, and the fiftieth day is the festival. The Greek word for fiftieth is pentēkostē, and it is the name the New Testament gives this day: when the day of Pentecost had come (Acts 2:1).

  • v17 "baked with leaven" — leaven is banned from the altar (2:11), and for the seven days of Unleavened Bread it is not to be eaten at all. Fifty days later the offering is two loaves made with leaven. They are waved before the LORD and go to the priest (v20); they are not burned. The year opens with bread that has had no time to rise and reaches its harvest with bread that has.

  • v22 the edge of the field — the law of 19:9–10, set down again in the middle of the calendar. The harvest festival is not complete without the part of the harvest that is not taken.

  • v24 "a remembrance with horn blasts" — zikhron teru'ah. Teru'ah is a blast or a great shout: it is the shout that brings down Jericho's walls (Joshua 6:5), and the shofar teru'ah, the horn blast, of the jubilee (25:9). This verse names no instrument, and it does not say what is remembered. The day is the first of the seventh month; nothing in the text calls it a new year.

  • v27 "the Day of Atonement" — yom ha-kippurim, and the noun is plural: the day of atonements. It is the day of chapter 16, set here in the year.

  • v30 "I will destroy that person" — every other penalty in the chapter is cut off (v29). For working on this day God speaks in the first person: ve-ha'avadti, I will destroy, and it is the only time the five books of Moses use this form.

  • v32 "from evening to evening" — the only place in the Bible that says outright where a sacred day begins and ends: at evening. The tenth of the month begins on the evening of the ninth. It is the order of Genesis 1: there was evening, and there was morning.

  • v36 "a closing assembly" — atseret, from atsar, to hold back, to restrain. The eighth day holds the people back one day more after the seven.

  • v40 "the fruit of splendid trees" — peri ets hadar. Hadar is splendor, majesty; the Hebrew names the quality and not the tree. The other three are plain: palm branches, leafy boughs, willows that grow by water.

  • v40 "you shall rejoice" — u-semachtem, and it is the first time in the Bible that God commands people to rejoice. Genesis and Exodus mention gladness; neither commands it. The command comes with the harvest in, living in booths.

  • vv42–43 "booths… when I brought them out" — sukkot. On the night they left Egypt, the first place Israel camped was a town called Sukkot, Booths (Exodus 12:37). The festival makes every generation live where the first night out of slavery was spent.

speech.text: Leviticus 23
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: The appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies — these are My appointed times.
The Sabbath
Work may be done for six days, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You shall do no work at all. It is a sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.
Passover and Unleavened Bread
These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy assemblies, which you shall proclaim at their appointed time.
In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, between the evenings, is the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall present an offering by fire to the LORD for seven days. On the seventh day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work."
The First Sheaf
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest.
He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, so that it is accepted for you. On the day after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.
On the day you wave the sheaf you shall offer an unblemished lamb a year old as a burnt offering to the LORD,
and its grain offering, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a soothing aroma; and its drink offering, wine, a fourth of a hin.
You shall eat no bread, roasted grain or fresh grain until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
Fifty Days
You shall count for yourselves from the day after the sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the wave offering: there shall be seven full sabbaths.
Until the day after the seventh sabbath you shall count fifty days, and you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of bread for waving, made of two tenths of fine flour. They shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

With the bread you shall present seven unblemished lambs a year old, and one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire, a soothing aroma to the LORD.
You shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two lambs a year old as a sacrifice of peace offerings.
The priest shall wave them before the LORD with the bread of the firstfruits, together with the two lambs. They shall be holy to the LORD, for the priest.
On that very day you shall proclaim a holy assembly for yourselves. You shall do no ordinary work. It is a lasting statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap all the way to the edge of your field, and you shall not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and for the guest. I am the LORD your God."
The First of the Seventh Month
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a rest, a remembrance with horn blasts, a holy assembly.
You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD."
The Day of Atonement
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"But on the tenth of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy assembly for you, and you shall afflict yourselves, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD.
You shall do no work at all on that very day, because it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
For any person who does not afflict himself on that very day shall be cut off from his people.
Any person who does any work at all on that very day — I will destroy that person from among his people.
You shall do no work at all. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall afflict yourselves. On the ninth of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your sabbath."
Booths
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths, seven days to the LORD.
On the first day is a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

For seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a closing assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.

These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, for presenting offerings by fire to the LORD — burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day —
besides the LORD's sabbaths, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your freewill offerings, which you give to the LORD.

But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall keep the festival of the LORD seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day is a rest.

On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
You shall keep it as a festival to the LORD seven days in the year. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall keep it.
You shall live in booths for seven days. Every native Israelite shall live in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
Moses told the sons of Israel the appointed times of the LORD.

chapters.title: The Lamp, the Bread, and the Name
chapters.html:
Leviticus 24

The Lamp and the Bread

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Command the sons of Israel to bring you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to set up a lamp continually.

3Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall set it in order from evening until morning before the LORD continually. It is a lasting statute throughout your generations.

4On the pure lampstand he shall set the lamps in order before the LORD continually.

5You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it. Each loaf shall be two tenths.

6You shall set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD.

7You shall put pure frankincense on each row, and it shall be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering by fire to the LORD.

8Every sabbath day he shall set it in order before the LORD continually. It is from the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant.

9It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy to him, from the LORD's offerings by fire — a lasting due."

The Man Who Cursed

10The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.

11The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name, and cursed. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

12They put him in custody until the LORD's decision should be made clear to them.

13The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

14"Take the one who cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.

15Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: Any man at all who curses his God shall carry his sin.

16Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall surely stone him. The guest as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.

17A man who strikes down any human life shall surely be put to death.

18Whoever strikes down the life of an animal shall make it good, life for life.

19A man who puts a blemish on his neighbor — as he has done, so it shall be done to him:

20break for break, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has put a blemish on a person, so it shall be put on him.

21Whoever strikes down an animal shall make it good, and whoever strikes down a human shall be put to death.

22You shall have one law, for the guest and for the native alike, because I am the LORD your God."

23Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they took the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The sons of Israel did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Notes

  • vv2–8 "continually" — tamid, four times in seven verses: the lamp burns continually (vv2, 3, 4) and the bread is set out continually (v8). Exodus 27:20 gave the lamp command to Moses; here the people are told to supply the oil. The light and the bread before God are never to lapse, and Israel keeps them going.

  • vv5–9 the twelve loaves — this is the bread Exodus 25:30 calls the bread of the Presence, lechem panim, bread of the face. It is set out every sabbath and eaten afterward by the priests in a holy place. It is the bread David is given at Nob when he is fleeing Saul (1 Samuel 21:7, the bread of the Presence), and the bread Jesus points to when the Pharisees object to his disciples picking grain on the sabbath (Matthew 12:4).

  • v8 "from the sons of Israel, an everlasting covenant" — berit olam, the phrase of the covenant with Noah (Genesis 9:16) and with Abraham (Genesis 17:7). The weekly bread is counted as one of the covenant's standing signs.

  • v10 "whose father was an Egyptian man" — the only story in Leviticus outside the priests' ordination (chapters 8–10), and it turns on a man of mixed birth, the kind Exodus 12:38 calls the great mixed crowd that came out with Israel. His mother is named; he is not.

  • v11 "blasphemed the Name" — va-yiqqov, from naqav. The verb means to pierce, and also to mark out by name: the men who were designated by name in Numbers 1:17. Balaam uses it for cursing: how can I curse whom God has not cursed? (Numbers 23:8). The Name, ha-shem, stands alone, without of the LORD, the first time in the Bible that God's name is called simply the Name. Verse 16 then gives it in full.

  • v14 "lay their hands on his head" — ve-samkhu, the verb of the offerer laying his hand on the animal's head (1:4), and of Aaron laying both hands on the goat for Azazel (16:21). Those who heard the curse put their hands on the man who spoke it before he is put to death.

  • vv19–20 "a blemish" — mum, the word of the last three chapters: the blemish that keeps a priest from the altar (21:17) and an animal off it (22:20). Here it is the injury one man does to another. Eye for eye, tooth for tooth is the formula of Exodus 21:24. Here it sits inside a law stated twice to be the same for the foreigner and the native (vv16, 22).

  • v23 "they did as the LORD had commanded" — the sentence that closes the building of the tabernacle (Exodus 39–40). It closes this story too. The law of vv15–22 comes out of a case that happened.
