chapters.title: The Sabbath Year and the Jubilee
chapters.html:
Leviticus 25

A Sabbath for the Land

1The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, the land shall keep a sabbath to the LORD.

3For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.

4But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath of complete rest for the land, a sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.

5You shall not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, or gather the grapes of your untrimmed vine. It shall be a year of complete rest for the land.

6The sabbath of the land shall be food for you — for you, and for your male slave and your female slave, and for your hired man and your resident, who live with you as guests,

7and for your livestock and for the wild animals that are in your land. All its produce shall be food.

The Jubilee

8You shall count for yourself seven sabbaths of years, seven years seven times, so that the days of the seven sabbaths of years come to forty-nine years.

9Then you shall send the horn's blast through the land, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall send the horn through all your land.

10You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty in the land to all who live in it. It shall be a jubilee for you, and each of you shall return to his holding and to his family.

11That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you. You shall not sow, and you shall not reap what grows by itself, and you shall not gather the grapes of its untrimmed vines.

12Because it is a jubilee, it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce straight from the field.

13In this year of jubilee you shall return, each man to his holding.

14If you sell something to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.

15By the number of years since the jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor; by the number of years of harvests he shall sell to you.

16The more the years, the higher you shall make its price; the fewer the years, the lower you shall make its price, because it is a number of harvests that he is selling you.

17You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God, because I am the LORD your God.

18You shall do My statutes, and keep My rulings and do them, and you will live in the land in security.

19The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live in it in security.

20If you say, 'What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our produce?' —

21I will command My blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce enough for three years.

22You will sow in the eighth year and eat of the old produce until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you will eat the old.

Redeeming the Land

23The land shall not be sold for good, because the land is Mine. For you are guests and residents with Me.

24In all the land you hold, you shall allow the land to be redeemed.

25If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his holding, his redeemer who is closest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.

26If a man has no one to redeem it, and he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,

27he shall count the years since he sold it, and pay back what remains to the man he sold it to, and return to his holding.

28But if he has not found enough to pay him back, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the one who bought it until the year of jubilee. It shall go out in the jubilee, and he shall return to his holding.

29If a man sells a house to live in, in a walled city, his right to redeem it shall last until a full year after its sale. For a year he may redeem it.

30If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city shall belong for good to the one who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not go out in the jubilee.

31But the houses of villages that have no wall around them shall be counted as the fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.

32As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they hold — the Levites shall always have the right to redeem them.

33If one of the Levites redeems it, then the house that was sold in the city he holds shall go out in the jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their holding among the sons of Israel.

34The pasture land around their cities shall not be sold, because it is their holding forever.

A Brother Who Becomes Poor

35If your brother becomes poor and his hand fails beside you, you shall hold him up. As a guest and a resident, he shall live with you.

36Take no interest from him and no increase, but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.

37You shall not give him your money at interest, and you shall not give him your food for increase.

38I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.

39If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him work as a slave works.

40As a hired man, as a resident, he shall be with you. Until the year of jubilee he shall work with you.

41Then he shall go out from you, he and his sons with him, and he shall return to his family and to the holding of his fathers.

42For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as a slave is sold.

43You shall not rule over him with crushing harshness, but you shall fear your God.

44The male and female slaves you may have are to come from the nations around you; from them you may buy male and female slaves.

45Also from the sons of the residents who live with you as guests, from them you may buy, and from their families that are with you, whom they have fathered in your land. They may be your property.

46You may leave them to your sons after you, to inherit as property. You may make them work for you forever. But over your brothers, the sons of Israel, one over another, you shall not rule with crushing harshness.

47If a guest or a resident with you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the guest or resident with you, or to an offshoot of the guest's family,

48after he is sold he shall have the right to be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him,

49or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or anyone of his own flesh from his family may redeem him, or if he prospers he may redeem himself.

50He shall reckon with the one who bought him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years. His time with him shall be counted like the days of a hired man.

51If many years remain, he shall pay back for his redemption a matching part of the price he was bought for.

52If few years remain until the year of jubilee, he shall reckon it with him; according to his years he shall pay back his redemption.

53He shall be with the buyer like a man hired year by year, and the buyer shall not rule over him with crushing harshness in your sight.

54If he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he and his sons with him.

55For the sons of Israel are servants to Me. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

Notes

  • v1 "on Mount Sinai" — the mountain is named here for the first time since 7:38, and again at the close of the next two chapters (26:46, 27:34). The laws of land, debt and release are marked as given at Sinai, alongside the covenant itself.

  • v5 "your untrimmed vine" — nezirekha, your nazir: the word for a Nazirite, the man who lets no razor touch his head (Numbers 6:5). The vine left unpruned in the sabbath year is called a Nazirite vine, set apart and left to grow as it will.

  • v9 "send the horn's blast through the land" — ve-ha'avarta shofar teru'ah, and the verb is avar, to pass through: the verb of the Passover night, I will pass through the land of Egypt (Exodus 12:12). The sound is made to cross the whole land. The shofar is a ram's horn, and the teru'ah is the blast of 23:24. The year of release is announced on the Day of Atonement.

  • v10 "proclaim liberty… a jubilee" — deror, release, the freeing of those held. Isaiah takes up the phrase for the one anointed to proclaim liberty to the captives (61:1), and Jesus reads that line aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:18). The Liberty Bell in Philadelphia carries this verse. Jubilee is yovel, the ram, and so the ram's horn: the horns blown at Jericho are yovel horns (Joshua 6:5). The year is named for the sound that starts it.

  • vv15–16 "it is a number of harvests he is selling" — land is not sold at all, only the use of it until the next jubilee. The price is the number of crops left, and the law makes the buyer count them.

  • v21 "I will command My blessing" — ve-tsivviti et birkhati, the verb of God's commandments. God does not ask the land for a harvest; He commands the blessing, and it yields three years' food in one.

  • v23 "for you are guests and residents with Me" — gerim ve-toshavim, the same two words Abraham used of himself to the Hittites when he had no land to bury Sarah in: a guest and a resident I am among you (Genesis 23:4). Israel is to hold the land the way Abraham lived in it: as a guest of the owner, who is God.

  • v25 "his redeemer" — go'alo, from ga'al, to buy back what belongs to the family. The go'el is the nearest relative, whose duty is to redeem the land, or the man, before they are lost. Boaz is the go'el who redeems Naomi's field and marries Ruth (Ruth 4:4), and Job says I know that my redeemer lives (Job 19:25). It is the same word.

  • v30 "the house in the walled city" — the Hebrew text as written says the city which has not a wall, lo, spelled with an aleph. The reading marked in the margin is lo spelled with a vav, which has a wall, and v29 shows that is the sense. It is one of five places in Leviticus where the written word and the read word differ.

  • v35 "his hand fails… you shall hold him up" — u-matah yado, his hand totters, ve-hechezaqta bo, you shall take hold of him and make him strong. The law pictures a man about to fall and a neighbor who grabs him.

  • v36 "interest" — neshekh, literally a bite, from nashakh, the verb for a serpent biting (Genesis 49:17; Numbers 21:6). Interest is named for what it does to the man who owes it.

  • vv42, 55 "My servants" — avadai. Hebrew has one word, eved, for both servant and slave: it is the slave sold in the same sentence and the slaves of Egypt. Israel belongs to God, and so may be sold to no human master. At the sea the people said it would be better to serve Egypt (Exodus 14:12). The law answers that they already serve someone else.

  • v43 "with crushing harshness" — be-farekh, the word for how Egypt made Israel work: with crushing labor (Exodus 1:13–14). It occurs three times in this chapter (vv43, 46, 53), and every time the command is that no Israelite may do it to another.

If you sell something to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
By the number of years since the jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor; by the number of years of harvests he shall sell to you.
The more the years, the higher you shall make its price; the fewer the years, the lower you shall make its price, because it is a number of harvests that he is selling you.
You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God, because I am the LORD your God.
You shall do My statutes, and keep My rulings and do them, and you will live in the land in security.
The land will give its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live in it in security.
If you say, 'What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our produce?' —
I will command My blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce enough for three years.
You will sow in the eighth year and eat of the old produce until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you will eat the old.
Redeeming the Land
The land shall not be sold for good, because the land is Mine. For you are guests and residents with Me.
In all the land you hold, you shall allow the land to be redeemed.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his holding, his redeemer who is closest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it, and he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,
he shall count the years since he sold it, and pay back what remains to the man he sold it to, and return to his holding.

But if he has not found enough to pay him back, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the one who bought it until the year of jubilee. It shall go out in the jubilee, and he shall return to his holding.
If a man sells a house to live in, in a walled city, his right to redeem it shall last until a full year after its sale. For a year he may redeem it.
If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city shall belong for good to the one who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not go out in the jubilee.
But the houses of villages that have no wall around them shall be counted as the fields of the land. They may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they hold — the Levites shall always have the right to redeem them.

If one of the Levites redeems it, then the house that was sold in the city he holds shall go out in the jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their holding among the sons of Israel.

If your brother becomes poor and his hand fails beside you, you shall hold him up. As a guest and a resident, he shall live with you.
Take no interest from him and no increase, but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
You shall not give him your money at interest, and you shall not give him your food for increase.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him work as a slave works.
As a hired man, as a resident, he shall be with you. Until the year of jubilee he shall work with you.
Then he shall go out from you, he and his sons with him, and he shall return to his family and to the holding of his fathers.
For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as a slave is sold.
You shall not rule over him with crushing harshness, but you shall fear your God.
The male and female slaves you may have are to come from the nations around you; from them you may buy male and female slaves.
Also from the sons of the residents who live with you as guests, from them you may buy, and from their families that are with you, whom they have fathered in your land. They may be your property.

You may leave them to your sons after you, to inherit as property. You may make them work for you forever. But over your brothers, the sons of Israel, one over another, you shall not rule with crushing harshness.

after he is sold he shall have the right to be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or anyone of his own flesh from his family may redeem him, or if he prospers he may redeem himself.

He shall reckon with the one who bought him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years. His time with him shall be counted like the days of a hired man.
If many years remain, he shall pay back for his redemption a matching part of the price he was bought for.
If few years remain until the year of jubilee, he shall reckon it with him; according to his years he shall pay back his redemption.
He shall be with the buyer like a man hired year by year, and the buyer shall not rule over him with crushing harshness in your sight.
If he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he and his sons with him.
For the sons of Israel are servants to Me. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

chapters.title: Blessing and Warning
chapters.html:
Leviticus 26

1"You shall not make worthless gods for yourselves, and you shall not set up a carved image or a standing stone for yourselves, and you shall not put a carved stone in your land to bow down to it, because I am the LORD your God.

2You shall keep My sabbaths and revere My sanctuary. I am the LORD.

If You Walk in My Statutes

3If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do them,

4I will give you your rains in their season, and the land will give its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.

5Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until the sowing. You will eat your fill of bread and live in your land in security.

6I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will rid the land of harmful beasts, and no sword will pass through your land.

7You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.

8Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.

9I will turn to you, and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.

10You will eat old stored grain, and you will clear out the old to make room for the new.

11I will set My dwelling among you, and My soul will not abhor you.

12I will walk among you, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.

13I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.

If You Will Not Listen

14But if you will not listen to Me and will not do all these commandments,

15if you reject My statutes, and your soul abhors My rulings, so that you do not do all My commandments, and you break My covenant,

16then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring sudden terror on you, wasting disease and fever that wear out the eyes and drain the life away. You will sow your seed for nothing, because your enemies will eat it.

17I will set My face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is chasing you.

18If after all this you will not listen to Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.

19I will break the pride of your strength, and I will make your sky like iron and your earth like bronze.

20Your strength will be spent for nothing: your land will not give its produce, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.

21If you walk with Me in hostility and will not listen to Me, I will strike you again, seven times over, as your sins deserve.

22I will send the wild animals among you, and they will rob you of your children, and wipe out your livestock, and make you few, and your roads will be deserted.

23If even after these things you will not accept My discipline, but walk with Me in hostility,

24then I too will walk with you in hostility, and I Myself will strike you seven times for your sins.

25I will bring a sword on you that avenges the covenant. When you gather into your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be handed over to the enemy.

26When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and ration it out by weight, and you will eat and not be satisfied.

27If in spite of this you will not listen to Me, but walk with Me in hostility,

28then I will walk with you in furious hostility, and I Myself will discipline you seven times for your sins.

29You will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.

30I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars, and throw your corpses on the corpses of your idols, and My soul will abhor you.

31I will make your cities a ruin and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will not smell your soothing aroma.

32I Myself will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who come to live in it will be appalled at it.

33I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw the sword after you. Your land will be a waste, and your cities will be a ruin.

34Then the land will be paid its sabbaths, all the days it lies waste while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and be paid its sabbaths.

35All the days it lies waste it will rest, the rest it did not have on your sabbaths while you lived on it.

36As for those of you who are left, I will bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will chase them, and they will flee as one flees from the sword, and fall when no one is chasing.

37They will stumble over one another as if before the sword, when no one is chasing. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.

38You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will eat you up.

39Those of you who are left will rot away in their guilt in the lands of your enemies, and because of the guilt of their fathers they will rot away with them.

If They Confess

40But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their fathers, in the treachery they committed against Me, and also that they walked with Me in hostility,

41so that I too walked with them in hostility and brought them into the land of their enemies — if their uncircumcised heart is humbled then, and they pay for their guilt,

42then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember, and the land I will remember.

43For the land will be left empty of them, and will be paid its sabbaths while it lies waste without them, and they will pay for their guilt, because — and only because — they rejected My rulings and their soul abhorred My statutes.

44Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them and I will not abhor them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them, because I am the LORD their God.

45I will remember for them the covenant with the first generation, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD."

46These are the statutes and the rulings and the laws that the LORD gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai, through Moses.

Notes

  • v1 "a carved stone" — even maskit. Maskit is from sakhah, to look: a stone made to be looked at, carved with a figure. Ezekiel uses the same word for the pictured walls of the room where the elders worship images in the dark (Ezekiel 8:12). Worthless gods, elilim, is the word of 19:4, which sounds like elohim, God, and means nothings.

  • v9 "make you fruitful and multiply you" — ve-hifreti… ve-hirbeti, the two verbs of the first blessing on humanity, be fruitful and multiply (Genesis 1:28), and of the promise to Abraham (17:6). The blessing that began creation is what obedience in the land brings back.

  • vv11–12 "I will set My dwelling among you… and I will walk among you" — mishkan, the word for the tabernacle, and ve-hithallakhti, the form of halakh that Genesis uses for God walking about in the garden (3:8). The last promise of the blessing is Eden: God living among people and walking there. Paul quotes this verse as God's promise to the church (2 Corinthians 6:16).

  • v13 "made you walk upright" — qomemiyut, a word that occurs here and nowhere else in the Bible, from qum, to stand up. The yoke's crossbars kept the neck bent; God broke them, and the people stood up straight.

  • vv18, 21, 24, 28 "seven times" — the warning comes in four rounds, and each round ends seven times more. Seven is the number of the sabbath and of completion; this chapter, which ends with the land's unpaid sabbaths, measures the punishment in it.

  • vv21–41 "in hostility" — qeri, seven times in this chapter and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. It is from qarah, to meet or happen, and it has always been read two ways: against (meeting head-on, opposition), or by chance (living as though what happens to them has nothing to do with God). The second reading makes God's answer, I will walk with you in qeri, mean: then I will leave you to the chance you believe in. The Hebrew allows both; hostility is the usual English reading.

  • v26 "your staff of bread" — matteh lechem, bread as the staff a person leans on to stay alive. When it breaks, ten households share one oven, and the bread is weighed out.

  • v30 "your idols" — gillulim, its first appearance in the Bible. It is built on galal, dung, and sounds like it; Ezekiel uses it in more than thirty verses. The word is an insult, not a description.

  • vv34–43 "be paid its sabbaths… pay for their guilt" — one verb, ratsah, to pay off or make good, for both: the land is paid its sabbaths (vv34, 43) and the people pay for their guilt (vv41, 43). The land is owed the sabbath years of chapter 25 and collects them in the exile. 2 Chronicles 36:21 cites this chapter to explain the seventy years of exile: until the land had been paid its sabbaths.

  • v41 "their uncircumcised heart" — the first time the Bible speaks of the heart as uncircumcised. Deuteronomy will command the cure: circumcise the foreskin of your heart (10:16).

  • v42 "Jacob… Isaac… Abraham" — the covenant is remembered in reverse order, starting with the latest father and reaching back to the first. Jacob here is spelled with an extra letter, Ya'aqov with a vav, one of only five places in the Bible with that spelling, and the only one in the five books of Moses.

  • v44 "I will not reject them and I will not abhor them" — ga'al, abhor, is the chapter's turning word: God's soul will not abhor them (v11); their soul abhors His rulings (v15); His soul abhors them (v30); they abhorred His statutes (v43); and at the end, even in exile, I will not abhor them. The last use undoes the ones before it.

chapters.title: Vows, Valuations and Tithes
chapters.html:
Leviticus 27

Vowing a Person

1The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

2"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When a man makes a special vow to the LORD by the valuation of persons,

3the valuation of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

4If it is a female, the valuation shall be thirty shekels.

5If the person is from five years old up to twenty years old, the valuation of a male shall be twenty shekels, and of a female ten shekels.

6If from a month old up to five years old, the valuation of a male shall be five shekels of silver, and of a female three shekels of silver.

7If the person is sixty years old or more, the valuation of a male shall be fifteen shekels, and of a female ten shekels.

8But if he is too poor to pay the valuation, he shall be made to stand before the priest, and the priest shall set a value on him. The priest shall value him according to what the one who made the vow can afford.

Vowing an Animal

9If it is an animal of the kind that is brought as an offering to the LORD, anything of it that he gives to the LORD shall be holy.

10He shall not exchange it or substitute it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does substitute one animal for another, both it and its substitute shall be holy.

11If it is any unclean animal, of the kind that is not brought as an offering to the LORD, he shall make the animal stand before the priest,

12and the priest shall value it as good or bad. As the priest values it, so it shall be.

13If he wants to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.

Vowing a House or a Field

14When a man sets apart his house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall value it as good or bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.

15If the one who set it apart wants to redeem his house, he shall add a fifth of the valuation in silver to it, and it shall be his.

16If a man sets apart to the LORD part of the field he holds, its valuation shall be by its seed: fifty shekels of silver for a homer of barley seed.

17If he sets apart his field starting from the year of jubilee, it shall stand at the full valuation.

18But if he sets apart his field after the jubilee, the priest shall calculate the price for him by the years that remain until the year of jubilee, and it shall be deducted from the valuation.

19If the one who set apart the field wants to redeem it, he shall add a fifth of the valuation in silver to it, and it shall stand as his.

20But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it can no longer be redeemed.

21When the field goes out in the jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD, like a devoted field. It shall become the priest's holding.

22If he sets apart to the LORD a field he bought, which is not part of the field he holds,

23the priest shall calculate for him the amount of the valuation up to the year of jubilee, and he shall pay the valuation that same day as a holy gift to the LORD.

24In the year of jubilee the field shall return to the one he bought it from, to the one who holds the land.

25Every valuation shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary. Twenty gerahs make a shekel.

What Cannot Be Vowed

26But no one may set apart a firstborn animal, which as a firstborn already belongs to the LORD. Whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.

27If it is among the unclean animals, he may ransom it at the valuation and add a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at the valuation.

28But nothing that a man devotes to the LORD from anything he has, whether human or animal or field he holds, shall be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is most holy to the LORD.

29No one devoted from among people shall be ransomed. He shall surely be put to death.

The Tenth

30Every tenth of the land, whether grain or the fruit of the trees, is the LORD's. It is holy to the LORD.

31If a man wants to redeem any of his tenth, he shall add a fifth to it.

32Every tenth of the herd and the flock, every tenth one that passes under the rod, shall be holy to the LORD.

33He shall not pick out good from bad, and he shall not substitute it. If he does substitute it, both it and its substitute shall be holy. It cannot be redeemed."

34These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

Notes

  • v2 "a special vow" — yafli neder, from pala, the root of pele, wonder: the verb of 22:21. The book's last chapter opens with the vow a person makes beyond anything required.

  • v2 "the valuation" — be-erkekha, literally by your valuation, but the your has frozen into the word itself and no longer means anyone. v23 proves it: ha-erkekha, the your-valuation, which is impossible grammar unless erkekha had become a fixed term.

  • vv3–7 the price of a person — a vow to give a person to God is paid in silver, and the amounts run by age and sex. Thirty shekels is the valuation of a woman here. It is also the price owed when an ox gores a slave to death (Exodus 21:32), the wage Zechariah is paid and throws away (Zechariah 11:12–13), and the sum paid to betray Jesus, which Matthew ties to those words (Matthew 27:9, where he names the prophet as Jeremiah).

  • v8 "according to what the one who made the vow can afford" — al pi asher tassig yad, as far as his hand reaches. The same law that sets fifty shekels for a grown man sets the poor man's price by what he has.

  • v10 "both it and its substitute shall be holy" — the man who tries to swap a weaker animal for the one he vowed does not get the better one back. He loses both.

  • v28 "devoted" — cherem, what is given over to God so completely that it can never come back into ordinary use: not sold, not redeemed. The same word names the spoil of Jericho that Achan took (Joshua 7:1). With property it goes to the priests (v21). v29 applies it to a person, and there the text says only that the person shall surely be put to death and cannot be ransomed; it gives no case and no further rule.

  • v30 "every tenth" — ma'aser, the first law of the tithe. Abraham had given a tenth of everything to Melchizedek (Genesis 14:20), and Jacob had vowed a tenth at Bethel (Genesis 28:22). The book ends by making the patriarchs' voluntary tenth a standing law.

  • v32 "every tenth one that passes under the rod" — the shepherd counted the flock as it went out one by one under his staff, and every tenth animal was the LORD's, good or bad, without choosing. Ezekiel uses the picture for God counting His people back from exile: I will make you pass under the rod (Ezekiel 20:37).

  • v34 "on Mount Sinai" — Leviticus opens in the tent of meeting (1:1) and closes on the mountain, as chapters 25 and 26 did (25:1, 26:46).

But no one may set apart a firstborn animal, which as a firstborn already belongs to the LORD. Whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.
If it is among the unclean animals, he may ransom it at the valuation and add a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at the valuation.
But nothing that a man devotes to the LORD from anything he has, whether human or animal or field he holds, shall be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is most holy to the LORD.
No one devoted from among people shall be ransomed. He shall surely be put to death.
The Tenth
Every tenth of the land, whether grain or the fruit of the trees, is the LORD's. It is holy to the LORD.
If a man wants to redeem any of his tenth, he shall add a fifth to it.
Every tenth of the herd and the flock, every tenth one that passes under the rod, shall be holy to the LORD.
He shall not pick out good from bad, and he shall not substitute it. If he does substitute it, both it and its substitute shall be holy. It cannot be redeemed."
These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.
